Allergies:
Lithium

Chief Complaint:
Bilateral lower extremity claudication, left greater than right.

History of Present Illness:
___ male who presents with short-distance claudication 
affecting both
lower extremities. His symptoms are worse on the left.  He is 
only able to walk approximately one-half to one block before 
having to stop and rest due to calf pain.  Once he rests for ___ 
minutes, he is then again able to walk the same distance.  He is 
particularly limited when walking up inclines.  He does not
complain of foot pain at night to suggest resting ischemia.  
There is no history of back problems or back pain.  He does have 
arthritis and previously underwent bilateral knee replacements, 
but does not complain of pain in the joints.  He underwent 
preoperative evaluation by conventional angiography, and this 
demonstrated an atherosclerotic calcified lesion in the common 
femoral arteries bilaterally.
It was elected to treat him in a staged manner.  Because the 
symptoms are worse on the left, the left side was treated first.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with bilateral lower extremity 
claudication who was admitted to the ___ 
___ on ___ for planned left femoral 
endarterectomy. The patient was taken to the endovascular suite 
and underwent left common femoral endarterectomy and patch 
closure using a  
Hemashield Dacron patch. For details of the procedure, please 
see the surgeon's operative note. The patient tolerated the 
procedure well without complications and was brought to the 
post-anesthesia care unit in stable condition. He had palpable 
distal pulses in his bilateral lower extremities 
post-operatively and throughout his hospital stay. After a brief 
stay in the PACU, the patient was transferred to the vascular 
surgery floor where he remained through the rest of the 
hospitalization.  He did well without any groin swelling. On POD 
1 the patient was given a regular diet which he tolerated well. 
On POD 2 he was able to get out of bed and ambulate without 
assistance, void without issues, and pain was controlled on oral 
medications alone. He was deemed ready for discharge, and was 
given the appropriate discharge and follow-up instructions.  He 
was discharged with home services for physical therapy and wound 
checks.

Discharge Diagnosis:
Bilateral lower extremity claudication, left greater than right.
